end.summary:
Interpreted position-time graphs as motion stories, with this still needing steadier checking.
Used slope on position-time graphs to relate position change to velocity; this was shown on practice and a why/new-situation question.
Used slope on velocity-time graphs to relate velocity change to acceleration; this was shown on practice and a why/new-situation question.
Used area under a velocity-time graph to calculate displacement.
end.parentNote: Ira practised describing motion from graph shape, using slope for velocity or acceleration, and using area under a velocity-time graph for displacement. They connected flat x-t lines with stopping, flat v-t lines with constant velocity, and steeper lines with greater rates of change. No specific mix-up was recorded; graph-as-motion-story interpretation still needs checking across more examples. At home, ask them to describe one x-t and one v-t graph aloud before calculating anything.
